User Goal / Topic: "So sánh các phương pháp diffusion cho robot" Language Mode: Vietnamese Paper analysis (PMRL notes): ### 3. DreamFusion: Text-to-3D using 2D Diffusion - **ArXiv ID**: 2209.14988 | **Published**: 2022-09-29 - **Authors**: Ben Poole, Ajay Jain, Jonathan T. Barron, Ben Mildenhall - **Problem**: Text-to-3D synthesis is bottlenecked by data and architecture: the breakthroughs in text-to-image generation came from diffusion models trained on billions of image-text pairs, whereas an analogous 3D approach would require large-scale datasets of labeled 3D data and efficient architectures for denoising 3D data, neither of which exist. Prior zero-shot text-to-3D baselines (Dream Fields, CLIP-Mesh) therefore guide a 3D representation with a discriminative image-text model (CLIP) rather than a generative image prior; because CLIP is trained only for caption-image contrastive matching, it can be exploited with adversarial, physically implausible renderings, yielding assets with flat geometry, texture painted on top, and artifacts such as multi-headed objects. A second challenge is evaluation: standard 3D metrics like Chamfer Distance (against ground-truth geometry) and PSNR (against held-out photographs) cannot be applied to zero-shot generation from arbitrary text prompts because there is no "true" 3D scene corresponding to a prompt, and the authors observe that existing CLIP-based metrics often yield high values even when texture is painted on flat geometry, failing to capture geometric quality. - **Methodology**: DreamFusion performs text-to-3D synthesis by using a frozen, pretrained 2D text-to-image diffusion model as a prior for optimizing a parametric image generator, requiring no 3D training data and no modifications to the diffusion model. The core mechanism is a loss based on probability density distillation — Score Distillation Sampling (SDS): the diffusion model defines an implicit distribution over images conditioned on the prompt, and its denoising score is evaluated at noised renderings x_t = α_t·x + σ_t·ε; the resulting gradient, approximately ∇_θ L_SDS(θ) ≈ E_{t,ε}[ w(t)·( ε̂_φ(x_t; t, y) − ε )·∂x/∂θ ], is backpropagated through a differentiable volume renderer into the parameters of a randomly initialized Neural Radiance Field (NeRF). Optimization follows a DeepDream-like procedure: the NeRF is optimized via gradient descent so that its 2D renderings from random camera angles achieve a low distillation loss, producing a 3D model that can be viewed from any angle, relit by arbitrary illumination, or composited into any 3D environment. Accurate geometry further requires a set of optimization refinements identified in the paper: (i) ViewAug — augmenting over a large range of viewpoints; (ii) ViewDep — conditioning on view-dependent text prompts (e.g., "viewed from the front/back/side"); (iii) Lighting — optimizing illuminated renders produced with a point light and Lambertian shading in addition to unlit albedo color renders; and (iv) Textureless — optimizing textureless shaded geometry (normal-map) images in addition to textured renders. - **Results & Metrics**: Quantitative evaluation uses CLIP R-Precision (following Dream Fields, Jain et al. 2022) on the 153 prompts of the object-centric COCO validation subset of Dream Fields — the accuracy with which CLIP retrieves the correct caption among a set of distractors given a rendering of the scene. Baselines are Dream Fields, CLIP-Mesh (which optimizes a mesh with CLIP), an enhanced reimplementation of Dream Fields using DreamFusion's 3D representation, and an oracle that evaluates the original captioned MS-COCO image pairs. Despite Dream Fields and CLIP-Mesh having the unfair advantage of using CLIP during training, DreamFusion outperforms both baselines on color images and approaches the performance of ground truth images. On textureless renders that probe geometry, the reimplemented Dream Fields performs nearly at chance while DreamFusion's geometry is consistent with the caption 58.5% of the time. Ablations progressively adding view augmentation (ViewAug), view-dependent prompts (ViewDep), lighting (Lighting), and textureless shaded renders (Textureless) show geometry improving with each optimization choice and a +12.5% improvement in full renderings; notably, the base albedo-only model achieves the highest R-Precision on albedo renders yet exhibits poor geometry (a dog with multiple heads), demonstrating that textured albedo metrics are deceiving. Qualitatively, DreamFusion generates coherent, compositional 3D scenes (e.g., "a hamburger", "a vase with pink flowers", "a matte painting of a castle made of cheesecake surrounded by a moat made of ice cream") that surpass Dream Fields and CLIP-Mesh, with a large gallery of 3D assets, extended videos, and meshes released at dreamfusion3d.github.io. - **Limitations**: Documented limitations are primarily evaluative and computational. Because zero-shot text-to-3D has no ground-truth scene, reference-based metrics (Chamfer Distance, PSNR) are inapplicable, and the paper shows that even CLIP R-Precision is unreliable: it often yields high values when texture is painted on flat geometry, and albedo renders can be deceiving (the base model scored highest on albedo R-Precision despite exhibiting a multi-headed dog), so geometric quality must be probed separately with textureless renders. The method optimizes a full NeRF per prompt via gradient descent rather than amortized feed-forward generation, making synthesis computationally expensive (on the order of hours of accelerator time per asset), and accurate geometry depends on stacking several heuristics (view augmentation, view-dependent prompts, illumination, and textureless shaded renders) whose omission produces artifacts such as duplicated object parts. The probability density distillation objective is mode-seeking — the generator need only match high-likelihood modes of the 2D diffusion prior rather than its full diversity — so quality and diversity are bounded by the frozen 2D prior, pointing toward future work on faster/amortized generation and geometry-aware evaluation metrics.
